4. Cluster number and initialization. A three-seed k=2-5 grid selected k=3 in 2/3 MIMIC-IV, 1/3 eICU-CRD, and 2/3 AmsterdamUMCdb seeds, with k=2 otherwise and poor mixing at k=4-5. Those fits retained 100 samples per chain, and we present them only as a coarse screen. In the prespecified full-length K=2 versus K=3 experiment, eICU-CRD retains an all-initialization exact agreement of 0.771 and ARI of 0.495. The two degenerate poor-fitting eICU starts strongly influence this median; restriction post hoc to the single nonflagged fit gives exact agreement 0.997 and ARI 0.990. Because that restriction is post hoc, it does not replace the primary result. In MIMIC-IV, all three initializations have similar mean deviance, yet one assigns approximately 14% of patients differently (ARI 0.612), confirming genuine assignment instability. The evidence supports recurrent broad trajectory patterns and a useful three-component representation, but neither a unique biological taxonomy nor completely stable patient-level assignments.

Before refitting, raw-event reconstruction established that the archived six-hour field represented the arithmetic mean of recorded events (99.993% exact agreement; mean absolute error 0.00064; one discrepancy among 14,846 evaluable windows). The documented-window sensitivity retained 1,043 patients and all three independent full-length initializations converged and met the prespecified stability criteria (median agreement 0.835; median ARI 0.523; median NMI 0.438). We note plainly that an ARI of 0.523 means roughly one patient in six is assigned differently; the trajectory shapes recur, individual assignment is only moderately stable, and we do not claim otherwise.

The stricter ≥50%-coverage restriction retained 415 patients (29.3%) and yielded no stable PW component in any of the three initializations, with up to 41.7% of component-mean chains showing high lag-1 autocorrelation. Table S16b measures what the filter does. PW patients contribute a median of 4 documented windows against 9 for RR; the filter retains 22.4% of PW against 31.0% of RR and leaves only 28 PW patients in the analysed population. This provides limited support for a stable third component, and the poor mixing is consistent with selection-related depletion. The result does not establish a single causal explanation and is not evidence that PW is absent from the full cohort.

The principal independent endpoint is 28-day mortality. We fitted cohort-specific binomial generalized linear models with HC3 robust standard errors, adjusting for age, sex, AKI stage at first diagnosis, log-transformed baseline SCr, and onset nonrenal SOFA score. Relative to RR, adjusted ORs for DR and PW were 2.89 (95% CI 2.41–3.46) and 9.89 (95% CI 7.73–12.66) in MIMIC-IV; 1.93 (95% CI 1.29–2.89) and 8.40 (95% CI 5.23–13.48) in eICU-CRD; and 2.03 (95% CI 1.59–2.59) and 5.56 (95% CI 4.03–7.67) in AmsterdamUMCdb.

In a restricted first-dose 24-hour landmark analysis among treated patients, response was not consistently associated with 28-day mortality: adjusted OR 0.592 (95% CI 0.331–1.060; P = 0.078) in MIMIC-IV and 1.129 (95% CI 0.567–2.249; P = 0.729) in AmsterdamUMCdb. Table S19 now reports the same three evaluated response definitions shown in Figure S14, including the absolute ≥200 mL definition; this sensitivity analysis was also inconsistent across cohorts (MIMIC-IV OR 0.592, 95% CI 0.331–1.060; AmsterdamUMCdb OR 1.117, 95% CI 0.559–2.229). The response-by-phenotype interaction was present in MIMIC-IV (P = 0.040) but not AmsterdamUMCdb (P = 0.785), and no phenotype-specific pattern replicated across cohorts. We retain these results only as exploratory associations in the Supplement and explicitly distinguish the analysis from a standardized furosemide stress test and from estimation of a treatment effect.

We also compared the exact-version replay of the archived AutoGluon XGBoost_BAG_L2 model with a simple six-variable multinomial logistic comparator using minimum and maximum SCr, minimum and maximum SCr/baseline SCr ratio, and minimum and mean urine output on the same evaluation splits. On external AmsterdamUMCdb, the archived model versus the simple comparator yielded macro OvO AUC 0.769 versus 0.769, balanced accuracy 0.528 versus 0.578, macro F1 0.504 versus 0.583, and multiclass Brier score 0.576 versus 0.407, respectively.
